title: Stability of input-output maps and their minimal realizations in state-linear, state-affine, LPV, and linear switched systems
summary: Stability is often assumed in learning and identification, yet it is rarely characterized directly from input--output data. We show that an input--output family admits a stable finite-dimensional state-linear realization iff it has finite Hankel-rank and its response decays uniformly with time; for state-linear realizable maps this decay is necessarily exponential. We extend these results to state-affine, LPV, and linear switched systems via suitable input-forgetting notions, and relate forgetting to decay of impulse responses (sub-Markov parameters).
